# MM-P2-L1-SB03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Scope
This manual covers preventive and corrective maintenance tasks for the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet identified as EQ-P2-L1-SB03. It is intended for maintenance technicians and shift engineers responsible for preserving media containment, blast performance, and safe operation in the hot-forge cell. Tasks include inspection of wear components, replacement of consumables, torque verification of critical fasteners, media top-up, and documentation of condition and corrective actions. Refer to design change notices and operating procedures for context: ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, SOP-P2-L1-01.

Background and rationale
The shot blast cabinet is subject to abrasive wear and heavy loading in the hot-forge process. Wear of the blast wheel liner and loss of media inventory degrade cleaning effectiveness and increase risk of component failure. Tightening and confirming critical fasteners prevents accelerated wear and unplanned downtime. Media top-up at the prescribed interval preserves shot flow characteristics and surface finish repeatability. Maintenance interventions are sequenced to reduce exposure to abrasive dust and to limit handling of hot parts consistent with SOP-P2-L1-01.

Tools
- Handheld torque wrench calibrated to traceable standard capable of reading the specified torque value.  
- Impact-rated socket set compatible with equipment fasteners.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P2-L1-01, including respirator and abrasive-handling gloves.  
- Clean containers and approved media storage sacks for recovered shot.  
- Inspection mirror and borescope for internal visual checks.  
- Magnetic pick and mesh sieve for checking media contamination.  
- Maintenance log forms and camera for condition records.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Verify work authorization under SOP-P2-L1-01 and lockout-tagout protocols before accessing the cabinet. Confirm that the blast wheel assembly is stationary and that drive power has been isolated. Use PPE specified in SOP-P2-L1-01 for abrasive handling and dust exposure.  
- Position collection containers and lay out tools on a clean surface to prevent cross-contamination of media.

Inspection
- Access the interior by opening the service access panel per machine guidance and visually inspect the blast wheel liner for grooving, thinning, or cracking. Use the borescope for areas not visible by eye. Inspect adjacent wear plates and the feed hopper for fines accumulation and contamination.  
- Inspect media for fractured particles, foreign material, and fines. Use the mesh sieve to separate fines and the magnetic pick to remove tramp metal. Record qualitative observations and capture images of abnormal wear patterns.

Liner fastener torque verification
- Identify the blast wheel liner fasteners and clean the joint surfaces to ensure accurate torque application. Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply the specified setting to confirm retention. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. If any fastener does not hold to the specified setting, mark that fastener for replacement and record the original condition and any signs of thread damage or loss of clamping.

Media top-up
- Evaluate remaining media volume and condition against operational feel and appearance. When media requires replenishment, add approved shot media from traceable stock. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Plan top-up activities to occur before media degradation affects process quality. When top-up is performed, blend new media with recovered media by sieving to remove fines, and document batch codes of media used.

Wear component replacement and alignment
- If the blast wheel liner shows excessive wear beyond acceptable limits per engineering guidance in ECN-2026-036, replace the liner using manufacturer procedures and alignment checks. After replacement, re-inspect adjacent wear parts and verify that fasteners meet the specified torque. Align the liner to maintain clearance to the impeller and housing to optimize shot trajectory.

Cleanup and verification
- Remove fines and dust from the cabinet and adjacent areas using approved vacuum equipment. Dispose of collected fines per environmental and plant procedures. Reassemble access panels and remove lockout-tagout only after completing functional checks per SOP-P2-L1-01. Conduct a dry-run blast under supervised conditions to validate media feed and cabinet containment before returning to production.

Records and examples
- Maintain the maintenance log for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 with entries including date, technician name, observed wear conditions, fastener torque confirmation results, media batch codes used for top-up, and any parts replaced. Attach photos of significant wear or damage. Example entry fields: equipment id, maintenance activity, findings, corrective actions taken, signatures. Keep records in the document control system and reference ECN-2026-033 for configuration history when part replacements alter fit or material.

Acceptance criteria
- Blast wheel liner fasteners must retain clamping at the specified torque setting. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. A verified torque reading within the calibration tolerance of the torque wrench indicates acceptance. If a fastener cannot achieve the specified torque due to damaged threads or distorted mating surfaces, the liner assembly is unacceptable until corrective repairs are completed and re-torqued to specification.  
- Media condition and quantity must support consistent blasting performance until the next scheduled top-up. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Acceptance requires that media be free of excessive fines and foreign contaminants so that blast pattern and cleaning efficiency meet production requirements.  
- Post-maintenance functional checks must show stable media feed, no significant leakage of shot from the cabinet, and absence of unusual vibration or noise attributable to misalignment or loose components. Any deviation from these acceptance criteria mandates corrective action and re-evaluation prior to returning the cabinet to service.

Related documentation
- ECN-2026-033  
- ECN-2026-036  
- SOP-P2-L1-01

Revision history and approvals
Record revision, author, and approval signatures in the document control system per plant practice. Ensure traceability of maintenance events for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and linkage to related ECN entries.
